body:
Crypto Commons Gathering 2025

August 24–29, 2025 | Commons Hub, Austria

About CCG

Among the events held at the Commons Hub, the Crypto Commons Gathering has always held a special place. What began in 2021 as a modest excuse for then-PhD researcher Felix Fritsch to bring together crypto-commons thinkerers from around the world in his own backyard has since evolved into an annual moment of (re)connection and reflection for a growing community, and for the many lived practices and experiments in commoning, degrowth, mutualism and post-capitalist economic worldbuilding it is linked to.

Over the years, CCG has welcomed activists, researchers, hackers, builders, artists, game designers and others, newcomers and “OGs” alike. It has shaped itself as a convivial and fertile space for people and projects working across and beyond web3 to cross-pollinate visions, trajectories and strategies for realising regenerative and cooperative infrastructures.


About CCG 2025

While remaining an unconference at heart, each edition has reflected the community's shifting priorities and aspirations. In 2025, the gathering enters its fifth year, presenting not only a space to collectively take stock of what crypto commons has become and what it still could be, but also a moment for the growing community to think and organize itself anew.

This year's edition marks a shift in infrastructure as well:

  • The Commons Hub has become a full-fledged event hosting organization of its own, co-led by brothers Felix and Emil Fritsch, with exciting expansion and ecovillage plans in the works.

  • The Crypto Commons Association, until 2024 stewarded by Felix Fritsch and Giulio Quarta, is being reimagined as a cooperative vehicle for organising and supporting events at the Hub and elsewhere, introducing and evolving peer-production values and frameworks around them.

What to expect

  • Gather with others in a convivial, off-grid setting in the Austrian countryside, whether you're reconnecting or arriving for the first time.

  • Explore key themes through participant-led sessions, including:

    regenerative and collaborative finance, MycoFi, community currencies, digital and crypto commons, open source, degrowth, post-capitalism, ecofeminism, multispecies justice, radical game design, speculative fiction, and more.

  • Participate in a fully unconferenced structure, with time and sessions treated as a collectively managed resource. Bring your ideas for talks, roundtables, workshops, prototyping sessions, board game nights, LARPs, etc., immerse yourself, find inspiration, and team up with others.

  • If you’re interested, contribute to the ongoing co-creation of the Crypto Commons Association as it transitions into an events-oriented cooperative, a DAO, or something in between.

More Infos & Tickets

HACK THE HUB

April 7th - April 21st, 2025

Join us for two weeks of rebuilding the commons hub, renewing its spirit and reimagining its future.

We invite all friends of the Hub to contribute with their skills, ideas, and energy to its physical, digital and conceptual improvement, and to celebrate its resurrection with three days of Easter festivities.

While we’re open to creative input, a few key projects involve:

Building bunk beds and other minor projects;

Painting a mural on the kitchen wall facing the garden;

Finishing construction works in and around the house;

Resetting veggie beds and expanding our garden capacity; 

Improving our digital infrastructure and exploring new functions;

Conceptualizing social protocols that foster stronger community ties;

Working with a shaman to cleanse the Hub of lingering negative energies.

 

Board and lodging are free, as we count on your help to get the Hub in shape. More than that, though, we seek your feedback on professionalizing the Hub while honoring the values of its surrounding community. Participation in this event will have a lasting impact, not just on the space itself, but also on its atmosphere and culture.

Let’s build, dream, and celebrate together—to a bright future for the Hub and its community!

SOLARPUNK POW

A Celebration of Resilience and Renewal

OCTOBER 5th - OCTOBER 12th, 2025

This spring, the Commons Hub invites you to the SOLARPUNK POW, a vibrant gathering celebrating the possibilities of regenerative futures. In the spirit of Erntedankfest (Harvest Thanksgiving), we come together to honor the natural cycles of life, work the land, and cultivate both community and resilience.

What’s Happening?

Get the FarmBot Running: Help us finally bring the FarmBot to life, automating sustainable farming practices and showcasing the power of open-source technology.

Prepare Garden and Fields: Join hands as we sow and prepare the fields of the horse farm for the upcoming growing season.

Strengthen the Hub’s Resilience: Together, we’ll implement agricultural practices that enhance the Commons Hub’s self-sufficiency and showcase regenerative methods for thriving in a changing world.

More Than Farming

SOLARPUNK POW isn’t just about agriculture—it’s a celebration of a holistic vision for the future. Expect a lively mix of:

  • Workshops and Discussions: Delve into themes of regenerative technologies, solar energy, and community resilience.

  • Permaculture and DIY Projects: Learn from experts in hands-on sessions to take your sustainability skills to the next level.

  • Morning Meditations and Nature Baths: Reconnect with your surroundings and set the tone for a day of meaningful work and play.

  • Evening Fires and Dancing: Share laughter, stories, and music under the stars.

Whether you're an idealist, a tinkerer, or a dreamer of a brighter future, SOLARPUNK POW is the place to connect, create, and cultivate a thriving world.

Together, let’s sow the seeds of a regenerative tomorrow. Join us!

Commons Climb

A Rock Climbing Community Gathering

September 26th (Fri), 16:30 - 28th (Sun), 20:00

Join us for a free weekend of alpine fun, forging new friendships, and imagining the commons hub as a unique gathering spot for climbers.

SIGN UP HERE

Whether you're a seasoned multi-pitch enthusiast, a sport climber, or just getting started, join us for Commons Climb—a laid-back weekend of skill-sharing, outdoor adventure, and community building at the commons hub.

This is not a formal course, but a chance to meet fellow climbers, exchange knowledge, and find climbing partners for future adventures. Together, we’ll share tips on local crags, training techniques, safety, and more—with sessions shaped by you. Expect:

  • Rock climbing (sport & multi-pitch)

  • Partner matchmaking (find your next climbing buddy)

  • Skill sharing (bring your expertise!)

  • Swimming in Schwarza (refreshing!)

  • Evening hangouts (campfire, beer, hot tub)

The commons hub—a climber-run space with cozy accommodation—is our home base. Even the cook sends hard!


AREA & ROUTES

The commons hub is located right at the entrance of Höllental, a narrow valley with more than 2000 climbing routes. There are multi-pitch and sport climbing routes for all difficulty levels.


PROGRAMME

Friday

16:30 - 18:30 Arrival
19:00 - 19:30 Welcome
20:00 Dinner
21:00 Campfire

Saturday

09:00 - 09:30 Ice Breaker & Warmup Games /w Ruben
09:30 - 10:00 Commons Hub Intro & Commons Teams
10:00 - 10:30 Climbers Matchmaking
10:30 - 11:00 Morning Session & Day Mapping
11:00 Lunch2go
after 11:00 Open Sessions
18:30 Dinner
19:30 Brainstorm on Commons Hub as Future Climbers’ Base
after 20h Hangout, Hot Tubbing

Sunday

09:00 - 09:30 Morning Session & Day Mapping
10:00 Lunch2go
after 10:00 Open Sessions
18:30 Dinner & Closing

Format note: This gathering follows an unconference model—meaning you shape the weekend! Each morning, we’ll hold a collaborative "Day Mapping" session where attendees pitch ideas, workshops, or propose activities (e.g., "I want to learn trad gear placement," "Let’s go sports climbing at Schattenreich," or "Who’s up for a stretching workshop?"). From there, we’ll match interests with volunteers, assign times/locations/resources, and build the day’s schedule together. Think of it as a climber’s bazaar: bring a question, a project, or expertise to trade, and leave with new knowledge, partners, and experiences. Flexibility and participation are key—so come ready to co-create!

Commons Teams: At our events, we organize attendees into teams to collectively care for the space and each other. The Fire Team manages campfire and hot tub, Kitchen Team cooks, Cleaning Team makes sure the kitchen is kept tidy, the Shepherds facilitate sessions ("Stretching is happening in 5mins - come join at the outdoor gym!"), keep a pulse on group dynamics and are a point of contact for attendees. This collaborative approach not only reduces costs but also fosters ownership and connection—because the event isn’t just for you, it’s by you.


What to bring

  • Climbing gear (ideally marked) including a helmet

  • Cars (we have some, but ideally 1 car per 4-5 persons)

  • If you wanna have alcoholic drinks or fancy snacks, please bring them yourselves - we only provide basic vegetarian meals, and there's no shop in walking distance.


COSTS

This first Commons Climb is free to participate. We charge neither for accommodation in our dorms (rooms of 4 and 6, with a female-only room available) nor for the jointly prepared vegetarian meals.

Think of it as our kick-off advertisement: a chance for you to get to know the commons hub, and for us to explore together how it might become a gathering spot for climbers in the future.


IN CASE IT RAINS...

...lightly, there are some overhanging climbing areas that are rain protected.

...heavily, we'll focus on skill-sharing & partying in our two event halls and envision commons hub's climbing future: sketching plans for the commons hub boulder gym.

Calling all climbers!
Gear up, show up, and let’s build this community!

Commons Christmas Chaos

COOKIES, HACKS & FAIRYTALES

Some come for the snow, some for the hacking — and some just to spend the holidays with kindred spirits. This Christmas, the commons hub in the Austrian Alps welcomes digital nomads, makers, wanderers and creatives for two weeks of warmth, play, and togetherness.

From 15–26 December, we’ll share the quiet joy of winter: cooking, baking, hiking, storytelling, Dungeons & Dragons and world-weaving by the fire. Between snowflakes, cookies, and fairytales, we’ll also be tinkering on techy creations that showcase our Valley of the Commons vision at our booth at the Chaos Communication Congress (CCC) in Hamburg (27–30 December).

A lightly held space for friendship, play, and shared creation — we shape this event together, one cozy day at a time. Little by little, our days weave together into something bigger — a journey we start here.



Hard Facts

  • Accommodation: beds in dorm 38,90€ / night, beds in double rooms 48,90€ / night

  • Meals: 10€ per night communal cooking contribution

  • Shared maintenance: help out with cooking, cleaning, fire wood etc.

  • Bring your ideas: games, campaigns, tinkering projects — let us know in advance if you need specific materials

  • Chaos Communication Congress (CCC): join our Telegram Group to coordinate ticket purchase (tickets can be tricky!)

  • Travel to & stay in Hamburg: we’ll travel together on 26 December via night train (from ~80€, prices rising!), and stay in a shared hostel room, both booked once CCC tickets are confirmed

  • Optional return to the Hub: 30 December night, possibly followed by a relaxed New Year’s celebration (31 Dec–2 Jan, TBC)

Sign up now to secure your spot!

VALLEY OF THE COMMONS
August 24 – September 20, 2026

Valley of the Commons is a four-week pop-up village in the Austrian Alps, where people come together to imagine and rehearse life beyond extractive systems. Rooted at commons hub and held by forests, mountains, and open skies, the village becomes a living commons—shared in work and study, in making and care, in governance and everyday life. Through conversations, workshops, residencies, and collective experiments, participants explore new ways of organizing economy, housing, technology, and decision-making in service of collective flourishing.

This is not a conference, but a slow unfolding. Mornings trace shared thematic paths—commons, future living, cosmo-local production, decentralized funding and governance—while afternoons open into self-organized sessions, collaborations, and quiet time. Life happens in between: shared meals, long hikes, fire circles, and late-night conversations under alpine stars. Valley of the Commons is a test of permanence—a temporary village asking what it would take to stay, and taking its first steps toward making that future real.

More info at https://valleyofthecommons.com

body:
Hack the Hub!

27 March to 07 April, 2026


The snow is starting to melt, the first inklings of spring are manifesting, and the garden is waking up from hibernation.

It's time to Hack the Hub again!

Same as last year, we're calling on friends and supporters of the Hub to flock to Reichenau over Easter, lend their hands during day and celebrate the birth of a new cycle at night. We offer a straightup energy exchange - 4 hrs of active work per day for food and bed while you stay.

Lots of projects big and small are already in planning, even if we just achieve half of them the Hub will shine as never before. As always, we are open to suggestions and the serendipity of our flow, but we do want to prioritize finsihable projects that give you the happiness of completing something and witnessing the difference that you co-created!

What to do

There is much to do in the garden, as is always the case, and we would like as many strong backs with green thumbs as possible to come. We could also benefit from construction/tool use skills, good eyes for design and shui and cooking abilities. However, anyone with enthusiasm and a willingness to learn is welcome.

Side back garden

The side garden bed will need to be prepared for tomatoes and then planted.

The big box to be prepared and planted with crawling plants (e.g. pumpkin, sweet potato and watermelon)

The small box with root plants (e.g. potato, garlic, onion)

And if you allow me to dream....

....making a living fence with arch doorway separating the back side garden from the main section of the backyard and then planting the climbing plants.

Compost corner

The compost needs some turning action, that means a lot of f*rking shoveling! Then we will cover the new heap and prepare a new compost cage and material store areas. 

Wall facelifts

The bathroom block facade needs a good puttying! Would be a big boost to insulation!

While we are at it and for those with fear of heights, we can putty the kitchen facade as well.

The courtyard facade also could use some love, the windows require a fine touch and artisanal competencies (which we don’t have...) Also there are many tiny flower beds that could use some love and attention.

Courtyard playground

Attaching a pole horizontally to the crown of the Linden tree, so that swings and ropes can be attached.

So if we are going to dream then I would like to make ninja steps to the crown where a platform is! 

THE DOJO

We would like to create a dojo dedicated to all the physical arts, that will be open for all to use, share, learn. We plan to hang various equipment (rings, climber’s balls, trapeze and rope/silks), set up bolt and pole for a slackline, beautify the open courtyard nearby (see below).

If we are to continue to dream a small climbing wall that leans over the mat. 

Commons Patio

This area could be so much more! First, clearing the space of the wood (i.e. bon fire anyone?) and dealing with the massive cement blocks! I am thinking of filling the space with antique farming equipment, which we fill with earth and flowers - this time of season I would suggest Nasturtiums and wild poppies. But all flowering kind would be welcome. Then we can setup chairs and tables when needed.

Still in the dreamworld... it would be amazing to pour the area map cement model and place it somewhere in this space! 

Museum gardens

The area behind the museum and patio could use some intelligent permaculture style design implementations. Something like a dedicated wood and grass compost area, living fences for camping potential and some tree root removal/transplant when possible.

This little side area could be cleared and those wagons used in some interesting way.

Bike shed cut-del-paste

Would be good to clear out the whole room and reintroduce the bikes with associated tools and materials to maintain them. 

Hack the Tub!

Last but not least is our beloved hot tub. This tub has warmed many a commoner while they shared music, ideas, drinks and bodily fluids. It’s the liquidity pool that shares it all!

The good old tub has unfortunately cooked its last commoner last year ☹ ! But don't you weep, we'll buy a new tub, to be set up during the Hack! Then, while it is filling and heating up, we plan on extending the stone platform to the right of the tub, and generally improve the area around the tub. With all this done we can inaugurate the new tub and enjoy directly the fruits of our labor with a well deserved dip.

What to bring

The spring time here can be chaotic and the temperature can fluctuate from blissful warm sunshine to flash snow! So we suggest you bring:

  • Work shoes (e.g. gumboots, throwaway shoes)

  • Warm clothes (I think one heavy coat should suffice)

  • House slippers (we would be happy to keep them after 😽)

  • Your best!

 contact

If any of this is tingling the part of you that gets excited then please fill out the sign up form here and prepare yourself to co creatively rejuvenate the hub and self! I’ll be there with a tool in my hand and a smile on my face.

WORLDPLAY: To be Defined

June 7–13, 2026 • Commons Hub, Austria

WORLDPLAY is an opening move for a network that explores the revolutionary potential of play. What changes when we treat games as ways of organising, not just expressing? It's a pop-up hub for prefiguring radical futures – economic, social and cultural – through fiction, design, performance and play.

The first edition issues a call to game designers and players, artivists, weird economists and utopian dreamers. Together, we will:

  • Design and play upon the canvas of the world

  • Scribble futures and materialise speculative artifacts from parallel presents

  • Compose living archives of/for radical imagination

  • Devise ways to hijack public spaces, cyberspace and realities themselves

Part experimental playground, part aspiring peer-to-peer guerrilla futuring network, WORLDPLAY channels underground postcapitalist desire by sowing counter-hegemonic fiction engines as seeds and games as social organisations.

Visit worldplay.art →

Boulder & Build

A Climbing and Community Adventure

July 18th - July 27th, 2025


Join us for an immersive event combining the thrill of climbing with the joy of hands-on creation! Together, we'll construct a bouldering wall and training facility beneath the museum's "flugdach" (flying roof)—a striking architectural canopy—while diving into the rich climbing culture of the area.

What to Expect

  • Climbing Skill Sharing: Hone your skills and learn from fellow climbers in a collaborative and supportive environment.
  • Explore the Routes: With over 2,000 climbing routes in the region, from sport climbing to legendary multi-pitch challenges, there’s something for every level of climber.
  • Multi-Pitch Adventures: For those seeking a thrill, tackle breathtaking multi-pitch routes and experience the awe of climbing high above the valley.

A Typical Day

Morning: Hit the crags and climb to your heart’s content.
Afternoon: Cool down with a refreshing swim in the crystal-clear waters of the Schwarza River.
Evening: Join the team in building the bouldering wall and training area, adding your unique touch to this community project.
Night: Unwind at the sweat lodge and hot tub, sharing stories and laughter under the stars.
Whether you're a seasoned climber or just starting out, Boulder and Build offers the perfect mix of adventure, creativity, and camaraderie. Come be part of something extraordinary—exploring, building, and connecting in one of the most stunning climbing destinations in the world.

See you on the wall!
